_comment: Mapped Bitwarden secrets that NO workflow requests, and deploy-time names the map
does not hold. check_bws_map.py asserts coverage in both directions; this file is the
only way an entry is allowed to be uncovered, and every entry's `kind` is RE-DERIVED
from the tree rather than believed.
WHY IT EXISTS. Measured 2026-09-02: 53 secrets were mapped and 35 requested, and the
18-name gap turned out to be an exact bijection with 'has no GitHub secret of that
name'. The shadow's left operand IS a GitHub secret, so a name with no twin has
nothing to compare against and no request line was ever written. That is a mechanical
consequence, not eighteen decisions -- but nothing said so, and nothing would have
noticed a nineteenth that was a real omission.
KINDS:
no-github-twin  the name, and every rename pre-image of it, is absent from
secret-reachability.json's console list. Goes RED the moment the org
secret is created, because the shadow then becomes possible and the
exemption must expire with it.
deferred        a real gap with a real fix that is not ours to make. Requires a
worklist id AND a hard UTC expiry, and goes RED on that date whether
superseded-at-runtime  a SUFFIX-built name the deploy script reads and then throws away,
substituting another region. Re-derived against that script: delete the
substitution and this reds, because the secret is genuinely needed again.
or not anyone looked. Never use this to quiet a name you could wire.
NOTE: write a retiring name in braced form (FOO_{EU,US,ASIA}), never as a bare token.
secret-rename.py matches whole tokens, so a plain old name in a `reason` is rewritten by
the very rename the sentence describes, leaving it claiming the new name points at itself.

AWS_SES_HOST.reason: SMTP endpoint hostname; the account server talks to SES over the API. git log -S finds one commit, the one that added the map entry.

AWS_SES_REGION.reason: Public data, already committed in the clear at regions.json:17,35,53. No workflow requests it and no deploy path reads the stored copy: cd-deploy-account takes it from matrix.sesRegion, cd-deploy-worker from vars.AWS_SES_REGION_EU, and only run.sh:1533 reads private/account/.env. It sits in the store as an inert leftover -- keeping it costs nothing and deleting it is the operator's call. (This reason used to argue it 'should never enter a secret store' while sitting in one, which is an argument for a deletion nobody had made.)

GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_SECRET.reason: no OAuth or web flow exists in console, account, renet or elite; CI authenticates as the App with its private key. Stored so the App's credential set lives in one place.

GITHUB_AUTOPILOT_APP_ID.reason: an Actions VARIABLE (vars.AUTOPILOT_APP_ID), not a secret, and unshadowable by construction: the comparator fails on an empty side, so a request line would turn the shadow RED. See autopilot.yml:58-62.

OBS_OTLP_CREDENTIALS.reason: pre-regional leftover holding ONE region's value; the deploy uses the regional trio below. One stored value cannot be compared against three genuinely different regional secrets.

OBS_OTLP_PASSWORD.reason: human-readable half of the collector login; everything consumes the joined OBS_OTLP_CREDENTIALS.

OBS_OTLP_USERNAME.reason: human-readable half of the collector login; everything consumes the joined OBS_OTLP_CREDENTIALS.

R2_TOKEN_AUTH_API.reason: the raw bearer VALUE of a Cloudflare R2 API token, the third artifact beside id and sha256(value). Unattributed; identify it in the Cloudflare dashboard before revoking.

SMTP_FROM.reason: customer-supplied on the onprem image (Dockerfile:147 sets EMAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp); Rediacc's own Workers default to ses.

SMTP_HOST.reason: customer-supplied on the onprem image; nothing in CI injects any SMTP key.

SMTP_PASSWORD.reason: customer-supplied on the onprem image. Spelled to match env.ts:123, which is the key the code actually reads.

SMTP_PORT.reason: customer-supplied on the onprem image; the Worker schema defaults it to 587.

STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY.reason: public by design and there is no client-side Stripe integration at all -- payment is server-created hosted Checkout, so no publishable key ever reaches a browser.

STRIPE_SANDBOX_PUBLISHABLE_KEY.reason: public by design; same reasoning as the live publishable key.

STRIPE_SANDBOX_WEBHOOK_SECRET_ID.reason: an endpoint identifier, and a useless one: setup-sandbox.ts:76-125 destroys and re-mints the preview endpoint on every run.

STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.reason: unsuffixed leftover holding the EU endpoint's value; deploys use the regional entries. The name is a homograph across three namespaces -- never find-and-replace across it.

STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_ID.reason: an endpoint identifier, not a credential.

OBS_OTLP_CREDENTIALS_EU.reason: REAL GAP. set-account-worker-secrets.sh:134 builds this name at runtime and _require_nonempty's it at :209; the rename points the org secret OTLP_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS_{EU,US,ASIA} here. Only `./run.sh rotation rotate otlp-eu` can create it -- the value is readable nowhere, so this is operator work.

OBS_OTLP_CREDENTIALS_US.reason: REAL GAP, as OBS_OTLP_CREDENTIALS_EU. Create with `./run.sh rotation rotate otlp-us`.

OBS_OTLP_CREDENTIALS_ASIA.reason: REAL GAP, as OBS_OTLP_CREDENTIALS_EU. Create with `./run.sh rotation rotate otlp-asia`.

AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID_ASIA.reason: set-account-worker-secrets.sh:123-131 reads this name and then unconditionally overwrites it with the EU pair whenever SUFFIX is ASIA, because ap-northeast-1 production access has not been granted. The org secret exists and is reachable, but its value reaches a deploy environment and is discarded. Operator ruling 2026-09-02: do not mint an ASIA IAM key.

AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_ASIA.reason: set-account-worker-secrets.sh:123-131 reads this name and then unconditionally overwrites it with the EU pair whenever SUFFIX is ASIA, because ap-northeast-1 production access has not been granted. The org secret exists and is reachable, but its value reaches a deploy environment and is discarded. Operator ruling 2026-09-02: do not mint an ASIA IAM key.
